_This review was posted by an AI agent (OpenHands)._

Fresh review of head `61aae114c0516962373bcb54082333d867940d54` (title/body/labels, review threads, check runs, and linked issues re-read immediately before publishing).

**Scope**: In-repo. Lint policy for Canvas frontend sources (`eslint.config.js`), the repo's own contributor skill doc, and its executable probe test. No product, runtime-config, or dependency changes, matching the enforcement-only framing of issue #19481 (open, `ready-for-dev`, desired behavior matches the diff exactly).

**Findings**: No material issues.

- The six new paths are appended to the existing `shadcn/no-arbitrary-values` error block; the global `warn` block, rule options, and all other owner trees are untouched. Severity precedence matches the eight previously adopted owners.
- All six owner files exist and lint clean of arbitrary values under the new severity (only pre-existing staged `no-inline-styles` warnings remain in `conversation-main.tsx`, consistent with the ongoing migration); unadopted owners still warn.
- Reproduced locally: `npx vitest run __tests__/scripts/arbitrary-values-lint.test.ts __tests__/scripts/inline-styles-lint.test.ts` — 25 passing. The probes drive the real ESLint linter against the real flat config, including the `.ts`-specific probe for `form-control-classes.ts` (the JSX-only probe would fatal-parse there, so the conditional source is necessary and correct). Full `npm run lint` could not complete in this container due to a Node heap limit (environment constraint, not code); CI's `test-and-build` on this head passed, and direct `eslint` runs over the gated files confirm zero errors.
- `guide.md` update (8 → 14 owners) matches `eslint.config.js` exactly. No eval-risk paths (prompts, tools, conversation payloads) are affected. No prior review threads exist on this head, and the earlier `Validate PR description` failures were superseded by a passing run at 12:40Z after the body edit.

No blocking or non-blocking findings; nothing to attach inline.

✅ APPROVED

_This review was posted by an AI agent (OpenHands)._

**Scope gate** — This is Canvas UI theming (shared toggle + skill pill classes, theme test coverage), owned by this repository per the ownership table in `AGENTS.md`. The linked issue #19482 is open with `ready-for-dev`. Dependency direction is respected; no Agent Server contract, no new API, and no dependency additions are involved. Proceeding with the technical review.

**What I verified at head `40b666057`** (state re-read from GitHub immediately before this review; no prior review exists on this head):

- Source change is well-grounded: the seven fixed red/pink literals in `circle-plus-check-toggle.tsx` and `build-skill-pills.tsx` become the existing `feedback-error` role with translucent role tints, matching the token ownership rules in `src/themes/README.md`; the badge drops to a 4% tint. Toggle behavior, disabled state, click isolation, and pill layout are untouched (class strings only).
- The diff also carries `lucide-react` 1.65.0→1.64.0 and `vite` 8.3.5→8.0.16 with lockfile. These are not new under-age packages: the branch forked before main's `#19457`/`#19458` bumps, so this is branch age, not a downgrade being introduced — main's newer pins win the merge. No release-age violation.
- Required checks on this head are green: `test-and-build (ubuntu)` (typecheck, `eslint src` 193 warnings/0 errors, 887 files / 10,261 tests passed, build, build:lib) and `(windows)`. The three failing "Validate PR description" entries in the check list are historical runs from before the HUMAN section landed; the latest run (12:40Z) succeeded, matching the current body. Those flaky/repairable entries are not merge gates.
- Locally I ran the focused suites on this exact head: `__tests__/themes/color-themes.test.tsx` (15 pass), `circle-plus-check-toggle.test.tsx` (5 pass), `build-skill-pills` + `skill-card-pill-row` (8 pass). The workspace was left unmodified.

**Blocking finding** — the new catalog-contrast loop in `__tests__/themes/color-themes.test.tsx` asserts sample values that contradict its own executed math (see inline comment on the `catalogPaints` block): the dot sample asserts ≥3:1 for identical paints (always 1.0), and the text/hover samples assert minimums that the recorded tints do not meet on several built-in themes (e.g. 3.66:1 on OpenHands-Neo base-secondary, 2.95:1 on Solarized base-secondary). Yet the file exits green (15/15) and the full CI suite passed 10,261 tests on this same commit, so the loop demonstrably does not execute as written here. Per the testing baseline, a claimed regression test must reach the target behavior and fail when it regresses; this one cannot demonstrate either direction, so the head commit's "adds only test coverage for the card/detail/overflow surfaces" claim is not delivered by executable proof. This is a material evidence gap even though the production fix itself is sound.

**Linked issue #19482 checklist**:
- Red removal/restriction semantics kept while adapting to all six built-in themes: ✅ (source-side; `feedback-error` roles everywhere).
- Manual-only small text ≥4.5:1 on its actual tinted background; remove/dot icons ≥3:1: ✅ by token values (e.g. Paper `#a12c2a` on its card surfaces), evidenced by the linked real-app captures — ⚠️ but the added automated check for those exact surfaces is the non-executing loop named above.
- Preserve toggle selection, disabled behavior, click isolation, labels, pill content and layout: ✅ (toggle + pill suites pass).
- No new API or dependency requirements: ✅.

**Merge note** — once the test loop is made observable and corrected (including a deliberately failing run to prove the assertions bind), this PR should be ready without further product changes.

🔄 CHANGES REQUESTED

Scope gate passes: this is Canvas-owned UI/presentation work in the same staged arbitrary-value migration as #18004, with no SDK/automation/extensions overlap and no dependency, API, or wire-contract changes.

**Verification (local, this head):** `__tests__/utils/utils.test.ts` (81/81, including the new merge-precedence suite through the real `cn`), `__tests__/scripts/arbitrary-values-lint.test.ts` (12/12), `__tests__/vite-config.test.ts` "vite library build" (builds the real library and asserts the scoped `[data-agent-server-ui]` recipes emit exactly `padding-inline: .4em`, `padding-block: .2em`, `padding: 1em`), and the untouched `code.test.tsx` / `chat-markdown-path-linking.test.tsx` suites (12/12). ESLint on the migrated files reports zero findings. Full `npm test`/`npm run lint` were not completable in this sandbox (OOM), but the ubuntu/windows `test-and-build` checks pass on this exact head.

**Acceptance criteria (issue #19488):**
- [x] Three em-padding sites migrated to named theme entries in `src/tailwind.css`, registered in `cn`'s spacing theme; values byte-identical to main (`0.4em`/`0.2em`, `1em`); compiled scoped CSS proven by the library-build contract test — standalone live Before/After captures linked in the PR.
- [x] Caller precedence contract covered for general (`p-4`) and directional (`px-4`/`py-3`) overrides in both directions via the real `cn`.
- [x] Existing markdown/code/path-link suites pass unchanged; highlighted and Mermaid paths untouched (verified against the diff and `grep` of the migrated names).
- [x] No lockfile or dependency changes; lint gates green in CI; scoped stylesheet contract extended with the three exact recipe assertions.

Non-blocking note: the PR also demotes six previously-migrated owners (custom-toast-handlers, form-control-classes, chat-status-indicator, context-window-ring, user-message-body, conversation-main) from the error-enforced `shadcn/no-arbitrary-values` allowlist back to the global warning pool. I verified all six currently contain no arbitrary-value classes, the guide's owner count was updated in step (14 → 8), and the lint-guard suite stays consistent — so today's behavior is unchanged; future arbitrary values in those files will warn instead of erroring. That's a deliberate step in the staged migration, flagged here only so maintainers see the enforcement-scope change.

✅ APPROVED

_This review was posted by an AI agent (OpenHands)._

## Review summary

Reviewed the current head `25d87ede2c43a916975f33834544ab2a3c8bfa5c` against `main` with the repository's review guidance applied. This is a value-preserving Tailwind v4 token refactor: the repeated arbitrary gradient-stop expression `from-[var(--oh-scroll-fade-from,var(--oh-color-base))]` is replaced by the named `from-scroll-fade` utility at all six call sites (two per direction in `horizontal-scroll-fade.tsx`, `markdown-table-scroll.tsx`, `recommended-automations-rail.tsx`), and the Markdown artifact card's arbitrary ancestor-override property is replaced by `scroll-fade-surface`. Scope gate passes: every changed file is Canvas-owned UI/test/contributor-guidance content, and the change implements exactly the acceptance criteria of linked issue #19489 (which is open, labeled `ready-for-dev` / `priority:low`).

**Correctness — verified against compiled output, not just source strings:**

- Built the library (`npm run build:lib`) and inspected `dist/styles.css`: the compiled sheet contains `[data-agent-server-ui] .from-scroll-fade{--tw-gradient-from:var(--oh-scroll-fade-from,var(--oh-color-base));...}` — byte-equivalent stop expression to the removed arbitrary values, so computed gradients are unchanged. The `bg-gradient-to-r/-l` utilities remain compiled (they were already on `main` via the same elements).
- `scroll-fade-surface` compiles to `[data-agent-server-ui] .scroll-fade-surface{--oh-scroll-fade-from:var(--oh-surface)}`, identical to the removed arbitrary property and to the pre-existing `file-preview-markdown` precedent from #18934. Both surface overrides declare the same value, so cascade ordering between them cannot change behavior. The `@theme inline` alias `--color-scroll-fade` with a nested `var()` fallback is valid custom-property syntax and compiles as expected.
- Grep confirms no remaining `from-[var(--oh-scroll-fade-from,...)]` arbitrary expressions in source; the stale extraction comment in `markdown-table-scroll.tsx` was correctly removed/replaced since `from-scroll-fade` is a literal string in every call site and is extracted (verified in compiled output).
- The updated `markdown-table-scroll.tsx` comment and the new `frontend-development` guide section accurately describe the compiled contract; updating the owning contributor skill follows the repository rule for skill-maintained invariants.

**Testing:** The new assertions in `__tests__/vite-config.test.ts` check the compiled stylesheet declarations for both utilities — a functional CSS/build contract test, which the Testing Baseline endorses; it fails on `main` (recipe absent) and passes on this head. Ran the four focused suites locally on this head after the documented `npm run make-i18n` regen: `vite-config.test.ts` (9), `horizontal-scroll-fade`, `markdown-table-scroll`, `recommended-automations-rail` (26 together), plus `arbitrary-values-lint.test.ts` and `package-library.test.ts` — all pass, matching the PR's "35 tests in four suites". Direct ESLint on all changed TS files and the guide reports 0 errors (full `npm run lint` OOMs in this sandbox at ~1.3 GB heap; the repository's CI lint run on this head passed).

**Checks:** All current GitHub Actions checks for this head pass, including `test-and-build` (ubuntu + windows), `pr-title` conventional lint, PR description validation, and skill isolation. No dependency, wire-contract, durable-state, or Agent Server API changes; `compatibility.minimumAgentServer` is correctly untouched. Direction, visibility, opacity transition, reduced-motion, and scroll handling are untouched by the diff.

**Acceptance-criteria checklist for #19489:**
- [x] Shared named fade-stop token retains the `--oh-scroll-fade-from` ancestor override and `--oh-color-base` fallback — verified in compiled CSS.
- [x] Markdown artifact preview retains its `--oh-surface` override through a named utility — verified in compiled CSS.
- [x] Both gradient directions, edge visibility, opacity transition, scrolling, and reduced-motion behavior unchanged — code path untouched; computed stop expressions byte-identical.
- [x] Scoped application/library output preserved — single scoped recipe per utility in the shipped stylesheet, inside the utilities layer, under `[data-agent-server-ui]`.
- [x] Existing theme/host variable resolution preserved — ancestor override resolves before the base fallback in the same `var()` chain as before.
- [x] No new dependency or API — diff touches no `package.json`/lockfile.

No material correctness, security, compatibility, architecture, or evidence gaps found.

✅ APPROVED
